name: Apulia
summary: A white field with green and red stripes recalling the Italian tricolour, the words 'Regione Puglia' in gold and the regional arms: an olive tree inside an octagon under six bezants and the crown of Frederick II.
origin: The flag was adopted in 2001 and changed in 2011 to add a sixth bezant after the province of Barletta-Andria-Trani was created in 2009.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: From the Italian tricolour; also the olive.

symbols.name: Octagon
symbols.meaning: Castel del Monte, the octagonal castle of Frederick II.

symbols.name: Olive tree
symbols.description: An olive tree in the centre.
symbols.meaning: Peace, brotherhood and the Apulian countryside.

facts: Castel del Monte appears on Italy's one-cent euro coin.
Apulia produces around half of Italy's olive oil.
clues: An olive tree inside an octagon, under six coins and a crown.
Its octagon stands for a castle built by Emperor Frederick II.
It gained a coin when a new province was created.
